text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - Jan Luptak, leader of junior coalition member the Workers Party (ZRS), said the planned restructuring of the banking sector is designed to cover bank fraud with regard to extending loans.
- Luptak said the upper echelons of ZRS would decide in March whether the party would remain in the ruling coalition.
- The International Court in Hague will open on March 3 a law suit between Slovakia and Hungary over the controversial Gabcikovo dam on the Danube river.
- Jozef Migas, chairman of the opposition Party of Democratic Left (SDL), accused the state secret service of carrying out activities aimed at discrediting him.
- SDL has presented a revised draft law indefinitely postponing banking privatisation. The party hopes that the law could be included on the agenda of the March parliamentary session.
- Opposition deputies have warned that the Exim bank's exclusion from central bank supervision could hurt attempts to keep the crown stable.

- French-Slovak GSM operator, Globtel, said it planned to have about 25,000 customers by the end of this year. Globtel said it had signed roaming agreements with operators in Czech Republic, Austria, Hungary, Poland, France and Belgium.
HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Stock broker ARDS has denied it has any conection with steel maker VSZ. ARDS was alleged last year of acting in concert with VSZ in its purchase of IRB bank.
- Hydro-construction firm Vahostav said it would launch a 400 million crown tranche of domestic bonds with maturity of up to five years.
PRAVDA - Italy's Merloni and multinational concern Elektrolux have shown interest in buying into white goods producer Calex.
SME - Damages to Slovak companies caused by the Czech rail strike are estimated at some 20 million crowns a day.
